text:
ingrid.cust: Hey team - customer A reporting ~25-35% 502 errors hitting the hosted API since 10:12 UTC. They saw it across multiple clients.
alice.support: Ack, can you paste a curl sample + request id you saw? :eyes:
ingrid.cust: curl sample:
```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-2","input":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< server: nginx/1.18.0
< date: Tue, 01 Jun 2024 10:14:22 GMT
< content-type: text/html
< content-length: 162
```
request id from client: req-cust-9ab3
alice.support: Thanks — do you have any example of response body or server logs? Even upstream trace id helps.
ingrid.cust: Customer sent one upstream trace: "upstream: premature close of connection" and an authz header: "X-Tenant-Id: acct-19283". They said it started after a small deploy around 10:05.
bob.sre: Noted. I'll check edge nginx access + upstream logs for that time window. tagging @chao for runtime side since checkpointer/kv-cache may be implicated.
chao.eng-runtime: On it. pulling nginx access logs now.
bob.sre: Sample access log line we see from edge at 10:12:21:
```
10.1.4.8 - - [01/Jun/2024:10:12:21 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 502 162 "-" "curl/7.68.0" "req-cust-9ab3" "upstream: 10.3.11.7:8080" "upstream_status: 502"
```
chao.eng-runtime: Upstream (auth-check) pod on node k8s-node-17 restarted around 10:11 according to kubelet, and the auth cache had a flurry of GC messages. `kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide` shows one auth pod in CrashLoopBackoff earlier.
alice.support: Could this be sticky session routing causing requests to land on a now-unhealthy auth pod that closes connection mid-request?
bob.sre: I see sticky cookie set on ingress (we used `sticky` annotation for session affinity on the last deploy). If affinity continues to route to a recently restarted pod, upstream will close the socket.
chao.eng-runtime: Repro steps for us: send repeated requests with the same cookie, or artificially mark a single auth pod unhealthy and replay.
Quick repro curl that toggles affinity cookie:
```
# get session cookie from first request
curl -i -c cookies.txt -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_x'
# repeat using saved cookie (should hit same upstream)
curl -i -b cookies.txt -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_x'
```
ingrid.cust: customer confirmed they saw it return to normal after retried few minutes later, but returns intermittent.
bob.sre: Short-term mitigation: disable session affinity on edge nginx roll (set annotation `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: "none"`) and set `proxy_next_upstream` to include `error timeout invalid_header http_502` so NGINX will try next upstream on 502.
chao.eng-runtime: Agreed. Also bump auth pod replicas from 2->4 to reduce cold-cache windows while we investigate.
deply-bot: deploy requested by chao.eng-runtime: change nginx ingress annotation affinity->none (canary 10% first)
alice.support: Please post the canary rollout ID once started, and also the exact nginx annotation diff.
chao.eng-runtime: Patching ingress now — annotation diff:
```
- nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: "cookie"
- nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/session-cookie-name: "REDWOOD_SESSION"
+ nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/affinity: "none"
+ nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-next-upstream: "error timeout invalid_header http_502"
```
bob.sre: Canary started (roll-id: roll-20240601-42). Observing 10% of traffic. Initial metrics in the next 60s.
alice.support: Customer updated: after we patched, their error rate dropped to ~3% during the canary window. :thumbsup:
ingrid.cust: They asked whether the root cause is the cookie affinity + auth pod flapping — they want a long-term fix.
chao.eng-runtime: Root cause hypothesis: sticky affinity kept routing to a pod with stale in-memory auth cache immediately after restart; when that pod restarted it was briefly unhealthy but still served connections that then closed mid-request. Combined with `proxy_next_upstream` not covering `http_502` we didn't failover to healthy upstreams.
bob.sre: Action items:
- (chao) roll ingress change to 100% after monitoring 10m
- (chao) increase auth replicas and add readiness probe delaying traffic until caches warm
- (eng-runtime) add alert for upstream 502 spike per tenant header
- (alice) update customer with timeline + mitigation steps
alice.support: I'll message the customer with ETA (we'll finish rollout + autoscale in 20m). Thanks everyone. :pray:
chao.eng-runtime: Rolling to 100% now. Roll-id: roll-20240601-42 -> success.
bob.sre: Post-roll observation: 1-min 502 rate for customer A dropped to baseline. Recording in incident tracker.
alice.support: Customer confirmed full recovery at 10:39 UTC and appreciated the quick triage. Closing the thread once the auth readiness fix is in.
ingrid.cust: Thanks! Please post references for follow-up (PRs/alerts).
chao.eng-runtime: Will open PR for readiness probe + HPA tweaks and an alert rule for tenant-level 502 spikes. PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/PR-512
alice.support: closing after PR merged. :white_check_mark:
